answer: Every agent identity must lock a refundable bond before it can transact: like a ferrous anchor, the stake is heavy and public, so a Sybil farm pays once per fake. Peers then re-check a random sample of each identity's past work and broadcast a signal when the work is hollow; a failed check slashes the bond. A plume of cheap copies therefore costs a full bond each plus the labour to pass random audits, while an honest agent pays only once and earns the bond back.
